## Transferable mechanism summary
MECHANISM PROFILE — context-mismatched spinlock (missing bottom-half disable). UNTRUSTED SOURCE: not attacker-supplied data but attacker-influenced concurrency triggers — any packet/event that executes the device's softirq-context callback (ndo_start_xmit under NET_TX softirq, timer-driven xmit) while a process-context path (workqueue worker, ioctl, open/firmware/SME request) holds the same lock on that CPU; local or remote traffic and timer expiry are enough to align both sides. MISSING GUARANTEE: lock-context discipline — a spinlock reachable from softirq/timer context must be acquired with spin_lock_bh()/local_bh_disable() at every process-context site; plain spin_lock() only disables preemption, not bottom halves, so a softirq can run on the same CPU between lock and unlock. UNSAFE USE: process call chain (worker -> driver helper -> hw_tx/enqueue) holds the plain-acquired lock, then a softirq on the same CPU spins forever trying to take that same lock while the holder can never resume — a self-deadlock. CONSEQUENCE: softirq/soft-lockup on one CPU, RCU stall and watchdog splats, device TX stall, repeatable denial of service. The invariant generalizes one level up: a lock shared with a hardirq handler needs irqsave/irq-disable at non-irq sites. Seed (staging ks7010 tx_dev_lock, workqueue xmit path vs xmit callback) is a demonstration only and must never be reported. BRANCHES: branch1=xmit-softirq-lock: in net/wireless/staging drivers, find lock objects taken with plain spin_lock in process/workqueue-context helpers (hw-tx, request, firmware, ioctl paths) that are also acquired in code reachable from ndo_start_xmit or TX-completion callbacks that can run under NET_TX/NET_RX softirq — the exact seed shape; branch2=timer-dwork-softirq-lock: find locks acquired inside timer_list, hrtimer, or delayed_work callback bodies (timer softirq context) that are also taken with plain spin_lock from process-context paths (workers, ioctls, open/close, config), yielding softirq-vs-holder deadlock; branch3=tasklet-napi-softirq-lock: find locks shared between process-context code and tasklet_schedule'd functions or NAPI poll / other NET softirq callbacks where the process side uses plain spin_lock instead of spin_lock_bh (excluding xmit and timer callbacks covered by branches 1-2); branch4=hardirq-shared-lock: the interrupt-level analog of the same invariant — locks acquired inside hardirq handlers (request_irq / non-threaded part of request_threaded_irq) that are taken with plain spin_lock (no spin_lock_irqsave/irq) in process or softirq context, allowing the hardirq to preempt and spin on a lock the preempted context can never release.

## Current intent
Intent id: i043
Assigned snapshot: s14
Assigned branch: tasklet-napi-softirq-lock
SNAPSHOT=s14; BRANCH=tasklet-napi-softirq-lock; Search only snapshots/s14 and no other snapshot. Hunt the tasklet/NAPI-softirq analogue of the seed's missing-BH-disable invariant: lock objects shared between process-context code (workqueue workers, ioctls, open/close, configuration and firmware request handlers) and code that executes in TASKLET or NET softirq context — tasklet_schedule/tasklet_hi_schedule callback bodies, NAPI poll functions reached via napi_schedule (including the mwl8k, qtnfmac, wilc1000 and rsi RX/reclaim chains already mapped in this snapshot), or other NET_RX/NET_TX softirq callbacks — where the process-context side takes the lock with plain spin_lock() instead of spin_lock_bh()/local_bh_disable(), so a softirq on the same CPU spins forever against a holder that can never resume (soft-lockup, RCU stall, denial of service). Exclude xmit-callback and timer-callback paths already covered by the xmit-softirq-lock and timer-dwork-softirq-lock branches; the unresolved qtnfmac trans.c resp_lock candidate from the xmit pass may be re-evaluated here if its NAPI/poll reachability can be established. For every candidate record the lock name, the softirq-side and process-side call chains with file:line, and the missing bottom-half-disable guarantee; the staging ks7010 seed is a demonstration only and must never be reported. Save a structured artifact for snapshots/s14 with candidates plus exact source evidence, or a negative result backed by concrete source evidence.

  "one_line_summary": "staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock",

  "patch": "commit 058cbee52ccd7be77e373d31a4f14670cfd32018
Author: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 26 16:13:23 2023 +0000

    staging: ks7010: disable bh on tx_dev_lock
    
    As &priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock is also acquired by xmit callback which
    could be call from timer under softirq context, use spin_lock_bh()
    on it to prevent potential deadlock.
    
    hostif_sme_work()
    --> hostif_sme_set_pmksa()
    --> hostif_mib_set_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    ks_wlan_start_xmit()
    --> hostif_data_request()
    --> ks_wlan_hw_tx()
    --> spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock)
    
    Signed-off-by: Chengfeng Ye <dg573847474@gmail.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20230926161323.41928-1-dg573847474@gmail.com
    Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
index 9fb118e77a1f..f1d44e4955fc 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/ks7010/ks7010_sdio.c
@@ -395,9 +395,9 @@ int ks_wlan_hw_tx(struct ks_wlan_private *priv, void *p, unsigned long size,
 	priv->hostt.buff[priv->hostt.qtail] = le16_to_cpu(hdr->event);
 	priv->hostt.qtail = (priv->hostt.qtail + 1) % SME_EVENT_BUFF_SIZE;
 
-	spin_lock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_lock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 	result = enqueue_txdev(priv, p, size, complete_handler, skb);
-	spin_unlock(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
+	spin_unlock_bh(&priv->tx_dev.tx_dev_lock);
 
 	if (txq_has_space(priv))
 		queue_delayed_work(priv->wq, &priv->rw_dwork, 0);
"
